$comment: Evidence-driven development: every claim p2pagents makes, and the evidence that proves it. Test ids are <target>::<path> as printed by cargo test with '::tests' removed (target: lib, bin, or an integration test file name). Live checks are names printed by scripts/live_test.py; a trailing * matches a prefix. Run: python scripts/evidence.py [--live]. See README 'Evidence-driven development'.

claims.claim: Agents authenticate each other by public key and refuse every key that is not on the allowlist, including peers learned through gossip.
Agents on different networks find and connect to each other over the internet using only their endpoint ids (no IPs, ports or --peer).
live: worker2 found worker1 by id over the internet

claims.claim: Allowlisted peers discover each other by gossip and chat is delivered to every connected peer.
Two peers dialing each other at once end up with one connection and no join/leave flapping.
Peers see disconnects; a task in flight fails cleanly when its peer leaves, and departed peers can't be delegated to.

Peer tasks run only in folders the owner shared with that peer, by default the profile's own .p2pdata folder (read-only). The agent's working folder and every other folder stay private, and folders are advertised to peers by name only, never by path.
live: boss's task ran in worker1's .p2pdata folder
worker1 refused a folder it did not share with boss

claims.claim: A peer's task gets the lower of the peer's grant and the shared folder's maximum access, so a coding folder can be shared writable with one peer while the data folder stays read-only.
live: worker2 wrote p2p_live.txt in its workspace
worker2 audited boss's task with its grant

claims.claim: A peer can delegate tasks only if allowlisted with --delegate, and only within its hourly limit.
Delegated tasks run on a peer that serves the provider and the result comes back; providers a peer doesn't serve are refused.
live: worker2 wrote p2p_live.txt in its workspace

claims.claim: A peer's task gets the lower of the peer's own grant (default read-only) and the shared folder's maximum; peers can't raise it.
live: worker2 audited boss's task with its grant

claims.claim: Each agent uses only its own profile's identity, accounts and private provider instances, never the machine's global sign-in.
live: worker1's Copilot instance used its own COPILOT_HOME
worker2's Copilot instance used its own COPILOT_HOME

claims.claim: Tasks can't read files outside the workspace or credential files inside it (Copilot and Claude), and secrets never reach the requesting peer.
live: outside read result back at boss

claims.claim: Writes need workspace-write access, stay in the workspace, and can't plant files that run code later (.git hooks, editor tasks, agent settings).
Only the tools of the granted access level are offered; web, MCP, memory and sub-agents are never available to tasks.
Shell commands need full access and run in an OS sandbox with no network and no bypass; obvious escapes are refused before they run.
The web UI is reachable only from this machine with the per-run token (DNS rebinding refused), sets a strict CSP, and runs tasks.
Every task a peer asks an agent to run is recorded in the profile's audit log (peer, provider, access, outcome, duration) without the prompt text.
live: worker2 audited boss's task with its grant
worker2 audited the refused request from worker1
audit logs hold no prompt text

claims.claim: When a task can edit files, its result lists the workspace files it added, modified or deleted (build output and .git ignored).
live: boss sees the files worker2's task changed

claims.claim: A requester can cancel a delegated task: the worker stops the provider run, frees the task slot and audits it as cancelled. Tasks of a requester that disconnects are cancelled too.
live: boss cancelled a running Copilot task on worker1
worker1 audited the task as cancelled

claims.claim: Running tasks can be cancelled from the web UI and show as cancelled.
The agent's owner sees the audit log in the web UI (token-protected, no prompt text).
The Claude/Codex bridge passes task fields, runs requests concurrently, and surfaces provider errors and bridge exits.
The command line definition is valid (no conflicting flags or subcommands).
